children: Tesla Inc. (TSLA, Financials), the electric-vehicle maker led by Elon Musk, is facing a widening gap with BYD outside China.
BYD accounted for 35.4% of China's passenger new-energy vehicle exports in August, while Tesla China's share fell to 7%. The difference is getting harder to ignore.
BYD exported 183,746 vehicles during the month, up 130.8% from a year earlier. Tesla China exported 36,119, down 45.5% from July.
Through August, BYD had shipped about 1.13 million vehicles abroad from China, compared with roughly 331,000 for Tesla China.

And those numbers do not capture BYD's entire overseas push. The Chinese automaker is increasingly producing vehicles outside its home market, meaning its reported overseas sales are already running ahead of China export figures.
BYD has also raised its 2026 overseas sales target to between 1.9 million and 2 million vehicles and expects more than 2.5 million in 2027. That matters as China's domestic auto market slows.

For investors, exports are becoming a more important test of which EV maker can keep growing when home-market demand weakens. BYD is building momentum quickly. Tesla now has to show it can stop losing ground before that overseas gap becomes much harder to close.

title: BYD Takes 35.4% of China's NEV Exports as Tesla Loses Ground
